explication:
## Purpose and Entry Points
magic-trace is a Linux/Intel tracing CLI that captures Intel Processor Trace control flow, reconstructs high-resolution call-stack timelines, and writes Perfetto-compatible trace files (`.fxt.gz`). The executable entry point is `bin/magic_trace_bin.ml`; command parsing and command dispatch are centered in `src/subcommand.ml`.

## Trace Collection Backend
The main backend abstraction separates collection orchestration from implementation details in `src/backend_intf.ml`. The primary implementation drives Linux `perf`/Intel PT via `src/perf_tool_backend.ml`, with capability checks and perf control-FD handling in `src/perf_capabilities.ml` and `src/perf_ctlfd.ml`. This boundary encapsulates Linux-specific process tracing, perf invocation, and snapshot acquisition.

## Process Attachment and Triggering
Tracing targets a process and either snapshots on termination/Ctrl-C or at selected function breakpoints. Process metadata and executable mappings are modeled in `src/process_info.ml` and `src/perf_map.ml`; breakpoint installation/use is in `src/breakpoint.ml` with native ptrace support in `src/ptrace.ml` and `src/ptrace_stubs.c`. Trigger/snapshot policy is represented by `src/when_to_snapshot.ml` and trace scope/filter choices by `src/trace_scope.ml` and `src/trace_filter.ml`.

## Decode and Call-Stack Reconstruction
Raw perf output is decoded into repository trace-domain events by `src/perf_decode.ml`, producing explicit results/errors through `src/decode_result.ml`. Call-flow reconstruction then applies call-stack compression in `src/callstack_compression.ml`, models time segments in `src/trace_segment.ml`, and records state transitions through `src/trace_state_change.ml`. This is the core semantic boundary between external Intel PT/perf data and navigable application call stacks.

## Symbols and Address Resolution
Address-to-symbol resolution is a dedicated layer: ELF parsing/interfaces live in `src/elf.ml` and `src/elf_intf.ml`, while `src/symbolizer.ml` coordinates symbols represented by `src/symbol.ml`. Native LLVM symbolization is exposed through `src/llvm_symbolizer_stubs.cpp`; OCaml runtime names receive special demangling in `src/demangle_ocaml_symbols.ml`. Symbol-selection logic for trigger targeting is in `src/symbol_selection.ml`.

## Trace Model and Output
The normalized trace model is defined by `src/trace.ml`, `src/event.ml`, and `src/real_trace.ml`. Writer interfaces decouple serialization from collection in `src/trace_writer_intf.ml` and `src/trace_writer_implementation_intf.ml`; the active output implementation is `src/new_trace_writer.ml`. The generated trace is opened externally in the browser-based magic-trace.org/Perfetto-derived viewer; the CLI itself does not host a UI.

## Language Integration and Native Boundaries
The OCaml library exposes a no-op-but-traceable stop indicator for application-triggered snapshots via `lib/magic_trace/src/magic_trace.ml`, with C linkage support in `lib/magic_trace/src/stop_stubs.c`. A separate direct backend, rooted at `direct_backend/magic_trace_direct_backend.ml`, provides decoding/import functionality and C stubs (`direct_backend/decoding_stubs.c`) for lower-level or interoperable use. The project is primarily OCaml, compiled with Dune, plus C/C++ FFI for ptrace, perf-adjacent functionality, timing, and symbolization.

## Operational Constraints
The runtime depends on Linux `perf` support and Intel PT-capable Intel CPUs; ptrace permissions and kernel tracing may require elevated privileges. Traces remain local: the CLI emits files, and visualization is performed by a browser client rather than a repository-operated backend service.
